data.failure_directions: G1:H1 [7,7,7,2] fails as a frontier improvement if its mean gap is not below 3.625921 pIC50 or its condition mean rises above about 0.797 Å; that would support interval-3=3 as the local functional endpoint on the [7,7,7,*] background. G1:H2 [7,7,7,4] improving below 3.625921 would refute the local-minimum interpretation at 3 and force reassessment of the interval-3 high side. G2:H1 [7,7,5,3] fails if it does not beat the merged leader or if condition rises above about 0.797 Å; then interval-3 release on [7,7,5,*] is exhausted at 5. G3:H2 [7,7,6,5] fails to add value if it merely ties or trails [7,7,7,5] with no condition gain; interval 2 would remain a weak condition-side lever rather than a functional lever. Interval 0 above 7 remains adverse on tested backgrounds, interval 1 above 7 remains refuted, and no local amplitude change has a credible Best route. G3:H1 and G4:H1 duplicate cached arrays and are not new executions. Remaining sampling rounds are 0, so all selected items are archive suggestions, not executed wins.

data.comparison: Rounds 1-5 merged for teacher 5nn4_SC2_A_1017__top2 (v16): fixed 25 candidates, new R0 restart before update 10, 25/25 valid in every executed arm. Band is anchored to the unchanged pool minimum 1.902796 A ([7,5,5,5]); upper edge 1.922796 A; every useful schedule is inside, so mean |pIC50-teacher| gap decides. Round-5 arms: [1,7,5,3] 1.919291 A / gap 3.201721 (G1 anchor, new nominal leader, margin 0.003505 A); [1,3,5,5] 1.919706 / 3.201724; [1,1,5,5] 1.912936 / 3.202976; [1,7,3,5] 1.918910 / 3.201777. The in-band frontier is a seven-arm tie spanning 9.6e-5 pIC50: 3.201721 < 3.201724 < 3.201752 [1,5,5,5] < 3.201777 < 3.201783 [1,7,5,5] < 3.201787 [1,3,5,7] < 3.201817 [1,5,5,7]. Interval 0 is the dominant functional axis with in-band optimum 1 tick: ladder 5->3->1 gives -0.0292 then -0.0167 gap, 2 costs +0.0184 gap for -0.0020 A, and 0 is a reproducible ~1.944 A out-of-band floor regime buying only ~0.004 gap. Interval 3: 5->7 buys ~-0.00065 A condition for +6.5e-5..+9e-5 gap on interval-0 = 1,3,5 backgrounds; its release 5->3 is now measured at interval-0=1, interval-1=7 (+0.000627 A for -6.18e-5 gap) and produced the leader. learning_update.next_action: Use H1 to continue the same release one legal step to interval3=1, and H2 to pair it with interval1 release so the interval-1 contribution is separable by H2-H1. Both are archived because remaining sampling rounds are zero.
learning_update.applicability: This teacher, these fixed 25 candidates, R0 restarts before update 10; a fixed-population ordering, not run-to-run noise and not a generalization to new starting populations.
learning_update.alternative_explanation: The 6.18e-5 gap gain could be one tail candidate's amplitude-locked branch reorganisation rather than a broad population slope; exact reproduction at another step would argue against a single draw but would not identify a molecular mechanism.

learning_update.prior_judgment: After round 4 the in-band leader was [1,5,5,5] at gap 3.201752, with [1,7,5,5], [1,5,5,7] and [1,3,5,7] effectively tied within about 6.5e-5.
learning_update.intervention: Ranked the newly executed [1,7,5,3] against cached in-band schedules using the unchanged band anchored to 1.902796 A (upper 1.922796 A).
learning_update.revision: The leader moved to [1,7,5,3], but the improvement is within the 0.02 A ranking tolerance and only 3.1e-5 over [1,5,5,5]; this is a tied frontier rather than a strong new direction. Mean gap still decides because all arms are in band.
learning_update.next_action: Compare archived H1 and H2 against 3.2017208. If either is at or above this bar, report no credible in-band improvement beyond the measured release edge rather than inferring a new direction from a near-tie.
learning_update.applicability: This teacher and fixed population; measured ordering, with generalization to new starting populations unmeasured.
learning_update.alternative_explanation: The ordering may be below this fixed population's resolving power, so several arms could be indistinguishable; the final comparison should not overinterpret a few 1e-5 differences.

learning_update.prior_judgment: Interval-1 release 7->5 was a small functional-leaning, condition-costing tradeoff measured at interval3=5 and interval3=7, but its transfer to the new interval3=3 background was unmeasured.
learning_update.intervention: Compared cached [1,5,5,5] with [1,7,5,5] and checked whether any executed arm isolates interval 1 at interval3=3.
learning_update.observed_result: At interval3=5, interval1 7->5 changes condition by about +0.000429 A and gap by about -3.06e-5. No executed arm isolates interval1 at interval3=3; H2 is the proposed matched test against H1.
learning_update.revision: The interval-1 release edge remains small, background-local and not separable from interval-3 release in H2 without the H1 comparison. It is not protective and cannot be assumed additive.
learning_update.next_action: If H2 and H1 were ever sampled, compare H2-H1 before attributing any gain to interval 1. Do not spend future budget on interval1=8/9 or other weak extensions without a new compensation question.
learning_update.applicability: Interval 1 of this teacher at interval-0=1 and interval3=1 or 5; a local interaction statement, not a universal time-window role.
learning_update.alternative_explanation: The interval-1 effect may be tail-carried or may interact with interval 3; then H2 would measure only a joint effect and need not improve on H1.

learning_update.prior_judgment: Pool minimum 1.902796 A set the band upper edge at 1.922796 A; the prior leader margin was about 0.0037 A and no reachable single-window lever was protective.
learning_update.intervention: Rechecked the band after adding [1,7,5,3] and compared the new leader margin with measured interval-3 and interval-1 release capacities.
learning_update.observed_result: Pool minimum remains 1.902796 A; [1,7,5,3] is at 1.9192907 A, leaving about 0.003505 A to the 1.922796 A edge. The measured interval-3 release capacity is about 0.00063 A and interval-1 about 0.00043 A, both below the margin. Floor arms remain about 0.021 A outside band.
learning_update.revision: The band risk is unchanged and unhedgeable by the two archived releases: both H1 and H2 are predicted inside the band, but neither can protect the leader if an unseen sibling lowers the pool minimum below about 1.898 A. No proposal is called protective.
learning_update.next_action: Read any final result against 1.922796 A before making a ranking statement. If a lower pool minimum appears, re-rank under the new bound and treat interval-0=7-9 as fallback in-band regions despite their much worse mean gap.
learning_update.applicability: This teacher and the frozen band rule; a statement about eligibility and ranking, not a noise floor or success threshold.
learning_update.alternative_explanation: If no sibling lowers the pool minimum, the band remains at 1.922796 A and the concern is moot; the current leader ranking is unaffected either way.

learning_update.prior_judgment: Best, top10 and mean gap dissociate; [9,5,5,5] held the highest Best while trailing on mean gap, so Best earned no promotion.
learning_update.intervention: Rechecked Best, top10 mean and mean gap for the new leader and the high-Best comparison arm.
learning_update.observed_result: [1,7,5,3] has Best 7.22018 and top10 7.09742 at gap 3.2017208, while [9,5,5,5] has Best 7.32099 and top10 7.13262 at gap 3.254718. The teacher pIC50 is 7.412205.
learning_update.revision: Best remains tail-concentrated and subordinate. The new leader does not win on Best, and a larger Best below the teacher does not justify a predicted mean-gap loss.
learning_update.next_action: Rank by mean gap inside the band and cite Best only as a secondary tie-break; do not promote high interval-0 or high-Best schedules on the bonus alone.
learning_update.applicability: This teacher, these fixed 25 candidates, R0 restarts before update 10; a fixed-population quantity with unmeasured generalization.
learning_update.alternative_explanation: A higher Best might reflect a distinct binding mode, but sparse chemical pose mappings prevent any equivalence claim, so the frozen priority order is used unchanged.
